title: Zakariyya's quiet prayer
hook: an old man with gray hair and no children prays in a whisper, and is given a son named Yahya
tomorrow: the messenger in the eastern place

segments.voice: Yesterday, fruit in Maryam's room that nobody brought. Your line was from Allah without measure. What turned up unplanned? Day seventy, the end of week ten.

Stay in that little room for a minute longer. Zakariyya has just heard the girl in his care say that the food came from Allah, who gives without counting. And something stirs in him. He's old. His bones are weak, his hair has gone white, and his wife has never been able to have children. For years that door has been closed, and he's stopped knocking. Food nobody brought, in a room nobody entered. And right there, the Qur'an says, he prayed. Not loudly. Not in front of anyone. The nineteenth surah, the one named for Maryam, opens with exactly this: an old man, alone, whispering.
screen: `AN OLD MAN IN THE ROOM OF PRAYER.` → `A DOOR CLOSED FOR YEARS.` → `RIGHT THERE, HE PRAYED.`

segments.voice: Pickthall's translation of Surah Maryam puts it like this: “When he cried unto his Lord a cry in secret.” In Arabic, nida'an khafiyya. A call, a hidden one. Why secret? Commentators offered a few reasons. A quiet prayer is closer to sincerity: no one to impress. Or maybe he felt a little shy, asking for a baby at his age. And listen to how he makes his case. My bones are weak, he says, and my head is shining with gray hair. Then the line that holds the whole prayer together: “I have never been unblest in prayer to Thee, my Lord.” In other words: every time I've asked, You've been good to me. That's his reason for hoping. Not his strength, not his record. Just a lifetime of being answered. He asks for an heir, someone to carry on the family of Ya'qub, someone pleasing to Allah. And the answer comes, through angels, while he's standing in prayer: good news of a son, and his name is Yahya. The Qur'an says no one had been given that name before. Zakariyya is astonished. How, when I'm this old and my wife is barren? And he's told: it is easy for your Lord. Then he asks for a sign, and the sign is silence: for three nights he won't be able to speak to people, though he's well. The man who prayed in a whisper is given days of quiet. Christians know this child too, as John the Baptist. And that closes week ten: two dreams in a cell, seven fat cows, a heart that doesn't clear itself, brothers at the gate, no blame on you today, fruit without measure, and a whisper that was heard.
screen: `A CRY IN SECRET.` · `MY HEAD IS SHINING WITH GRAY HAIR.` · `NEVER UNBLEST IN PRAYER TO THEE.` · `A SON NAMED YAHYA, AND A SILENCE.` · then, large: `HE CALLED IN SECRET.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Think of one thing you've quietly given up on. A hope you stopped mentioning. A person you stopped expecting to change. A door you stopped knocking on. Don't argue with it. Just name it, inside. If you pray, you can ask for it again, quietly, the way Zakariyya did, with no one listening. If you don't, just let yourself hope for it for two minutes, without defending the hope. The bell holds the time.
Zakariyya's quiet prayer. An old man's hidden call, nida'an khafiyya, whispered where no one could hear, and answered with a son called Yahya.
Your line: he called in secret. Once today, ask for something without telling anyone you asked. Ten weeks on the path. Tomorrow, an angel comes to Maryam. Day seventy.

screen: `DAY 70 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE MESSENGER IN THE EASTERN PLACE.`

howItsDone: Muslims make du'a aloud and in private; Zakariyya's prayer for a child, in Surah Maryam, Surah Al 'Imran and Surah Al-Anbiya (21:89), is one that couples hoping for a child sometimes recite.

fork.setup: Zakariyya is old, his wife has never had children, and he has just seen food in Maryam's room that no one brought. what does he do?
options: announce to everyone that a miracle is coming.
fork.reveal: right there he prayed (3:38), a cry in secret (19:3). the answer: a son named Yahya.

original.note: Arabic, Qur'an 19:3: a hidden call, a secret cry.

trapdoor: what you thought: an old man gets a miracle baby.
what it means: a man who had stopped asking asks again, quietly, because he has never been let down in prayer.
what a scholar hears: nida'an khafiyya, a hidden call. commentators read the quietness as sincerity, and the three days of silence that follow as a sign fitted to a man who prayed in a whisper.

notes: Pickthall 19:3 and 19:4 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording.

The script paraphrases 19:4 as 'my head is shining with gray hair' (American spelling; Pickthall has 'grey'). The screen head uses the paraphrase too; confirm this is acceptable outside quotation marks.
The hook joins 3:37–38 ('there Zakariyya prayed') to 19:2–7; the framing that he had 'stopped knocking' is interpretive. Confirm.
19:7 'no one had been given that name before': commentators differ on whether it means the name or the like of him. Stated as the Qur'an says it. Confirm.
Reasons for the secret prayer (sincerity; shyness at his age) summarized from tafsir; confirm.
